decision: okf-foundation D18 (supersedes D3): the v1 type vocabulary is closed at NINE slug-cased namespaced types — bee.area, bee.feature, bee.work-item, bee.plan, bee.delivery, bee.decision, bee.pattern, bee.runbook, bee.evidence. Pitfall is not a type: it is bee.pattern with bee.polarity practice|pitfall
rationale: The owner's set with two adjustments: pattern and pitfall carry identical metadata and identical consumption, so two types would double the vocabulary to encode one polarity bit; slug case because the value is a CLI filter that must not need shell quoting. bee.guide/bee.overview/bee.reference are dropped with the legacy trees they existed to type

decision: okf-foundation D19 (supersedes D5): concept frontmatter is the five OKF recommended fields plus a nested bee: object carrying id (stable, globally unique, never reused, NEVER derived from the path), lifecycle (draft|active|superseded|archived), areas, required_context (bundle-relative paths), decisions; per type lane, polarity, critical, supersedes/superseded_by
rationale: Owner correction: bee.id is identity, not the path. Both are needed — OKF links are path-based (SPEC 5) so a foreign consumer can follow them, while a stable id survives the file splits and moves this migration performs constantly. required_context holds paths, not ids, so it resolves without bee

decision: okf-foundation D20 (supersedes D6): migration AUTHORS new concepts and RETIRES the source; it never annotates a legacy file in place. Per area: read the legacy doc, split it into concepts under docs/knowledge/areas/<area>/, carry its frontmatter values into the new concepts, then replace the legacy file with a pointer stub naming the new location. Legacy files are not deleted in this feature
rationale: A pointer stub keeps inject.mjs spec counting, the bee.mjs:1897 spec-debt guard, reading-map.md and every skill reference working through the migration — replacement without a flag day. Deleting stubs is F2's job, after every consumer has moved

decision: okf-foundation D21 (supersedes D7): bee knowledge index generates index.md at EVERY directory level inside the bundle plus the root index.md (sole carrier of okf_version 0.1), byte-identically from concept frontmatter, each carrying an HTML-comment provenance header. The critical-patterns.md equivalent becomes a generated index over bee.critical: true, never a hand-maintained file
rationale: Inside a curated bundle, per-level indexes are the progressive-disclosure mechanism the consumer walks; the 133-file objection applied to the legacy tree, which is no longer indexed at all. A hand-maintained critical list drifts, a generated one cannot. Frontmatter in a non-root index.md is an OKF error, so provenance must be a comment

decision: okf-foundation D22 (supersedes D8): scope INCLUDES the consumer. Ships: the Bee OKF Profile spec, knowledge.mjs + template mirror, bee knowledge check|index|list|context, the migrator, the docs/knowledge skeleton, the workflow-state area migrated end-to-end, the work-item/plan/delivery templates, and knowledge check joining the verify chain as a normal chain-failing suite graduated by D4's error/warning split. Deferred to F2/F3: the remaining 11 areas, work-item migration, promote, stale, links, stub deletion, skill rewiring
rationale: Owner correction: without the context-selection step, OKF only organises files and does not fix Codex degradation after compaction. A format without a consumer is a directory rename. Separately the ledger_parity report-only precedent was miscited and is withdrawn — that suite is chain-failing (run_verify.mjs:64, runCheck returns 1)

decision: okf-foundation D23 (withdraws D9, supersedes D14): a concept is any non-reserved .md file INSIDE docs/knowledge/. Files outside the bundle are not concepts, are not checked, and carry no frontmatter obligation. There is no in-place retrofit and nothing is stamped across the legacy tree
rationale: Conformance over a curated set is real; conformance over an archive is bookkeeping. This single move removes the 593-file retrofit, the 14 prose-header learnings, the filename-with-spaces hazard, and the timestamp double-source conflict that review loop 1 raised as blockers

decision: okf-foundation D11: docs/decisions/index.md keeps its path, owner and shape — one generated path has exactly one generator (bee decisions render); bee knowledge index never writes it
rationale: bee-planning cites it as the complete-by-construction decision-recall surface; under D17 it also sits outside the bundle, so no conformance rule reaches it

decision: okf-foundation D12: no new runtime dependency — knowledge.mjs ships its own frontmatter parser covering exactly the YAML subset the profile emits, failing loudly outside it rather than guessing
rationale: bee vendors zero dependencies; a parser that silently coerces is how metadata rot begins. Because the bundle is authored fresh (D20) the subset is one bee controls — strictly easier than parsing 113 legacy files

decision: okf-foundation D13: every knowledge verb supports --json; check --json returns {okf:{errors},profile:{warnings},counts} and exits non-zero only on OKF errors, or on any finding under --strict
rationale: The command surface is a Claude-Code tool-schema manifest; a verb without --json is invisible to it

decision: okf-foundation D15: bee knowledge list [--type][--lifecycle][--area][--json] emits one row per concept — path, id, type, lifecycle, title — and never file content
rationale: It is the primitive the context consumer (D27) is built from; defining it separately keeps query flags off check and index

decision: okf-foundation D24: the migrator lives in scripts/ (bee-repo tooling), not shipped to hosts; knowledge.mjs and the knowledge command group DO ship via .bee/bin/lib/ and must be mirrored into skills/bee-hive/templates/lib/
rationale: scripts/test_lib_mirror.mjs asserts templates/lib <-> .bee/bin/lib parity, so the mirror is an obligation not an option; tests under templates/tests are discovered by run_verify, a separate guarantee. Host-repo adoption is its own feature

decision: okf-foundation D25: docs/specs/workflow-state.md (1392 lines) is the proof area, split into docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/ as index.md + overview, gates, cells, handoff, recovery. EXACTLY ONE area is migrated in this feature
rationale: The owner named it and it is the worst case — largest spec, read by the most skills. If the loop works here it works anywhere. One area not twelve keeps the feature reviewable and the risk bounded

decision: okf-foundation D26: a feature's document budget is AT MOST THREE concepts — work-item.md (absorbing CONTEXT.md + approach.md), plan.md (standard/high-risk only; in tiny/small the plan is a section inside the work item), delivery.md (absorbing walkthrough.md). implement-plan.md is RETIRED as a committed artifact and becomes a render-on-demand view
rationale: bee-briefing already defines implement-plan.md as a projection; committing a projection is how two artifacts come to claim the same truth. This is the 5-7 to <=3 reduction, and it is why migration reduces load instead of renaming it

decision: okf-foundation D27: bee knowledge context --work <id> --budget <tokens> resolves the work item, walks required_context TRANSITIVELY, adds active decisions for its areas and every bee.critical pattern, ranks, and cuts at budget — returning an ordered MANIFEST of paths with size estimates and an inclusion reason per entry, never file content. Budget is estimated as bytes/4 and the estimator is named in the output
rationale: A manifest keeps the tool cheap, keeps the agent in control of what it reads, and makes selection auditable. Bee vendors no tokenizer, so the estimate must be declared as an estimate rather than dressed up as a count

decision: okf-foundation D28: exactly one concept may be authoritative for a subject — bee.id is globally unique, and an areas/<slug>/ directory has exactly one bee.area concept whose id is <slug>. Duplicates are a profile error under --strict, a warning otherwise
rationale: The owner's rule that two artifacts must never both claim to be the source of truth needs a mechanical form, or it is prose that decays

decision: okf-foundation D29 (supersedes D25): F1's proof area is docs/specs/advisor-protocol.md (202 lines) — same nine-section BA template as workflow-state.md, same area/updated/sources/decisions/coverage frontmatter, one-seventh the size. workflow-state.md moves to F2
rationale: Review loop 2 proved workflow-state.md is 1464 lines with only 11 top-level headings — a BA template, not topics — so the five proposed concepts left ~700 lines homeless, multi-session coordination (the second-largest cluster, ~207 lines) having no destination at all. advisor-protocol exercises every migration path without betting the feature on a 1464-line re-authoring

decision: okf-foundation D30: the workflow-state.md decomposition is LOCKED HERE as F2's input — nine concepts: overview (Purpose+Entry Points+Data Dictionary+Actors ~93), gates (B1,B2,B9a,B19,Closing-a-feature :534-581 ~91), cells (B7,B10,B17,B18,B23,B25-B32,B34-B36 ~254), handoff (B15,B16 ~47), recovery (B33 :699-752 ~54), multi-session (B11-B14 :237-324 + B20-B24 :415-533 ~207), review-sessions (B3-B6 :110-151 ~42), dispatch (B8 :167-185 ~19), advisor-consult (B9 :186-206 ~21). The 58 R-rules, 25 edge cases, hardening settlements and 20 Pointer bullets are DISTRIBUTED to the concept each governs, never collected into a dumping-ground concept
rationale: Derived from real line anchors during review loop 2. Locking it now means F2 inherits a decomposition instead of re-deriving one, and makes explicit that a heading-based split does not work on a BA-template spec

decision: okf-foundation D31 (supersedes D28): bee.area types EVERY current-truth concept about a subsystem, several per areas/<slug>/ directory. Uniqueness is enforced on bee.id (globally unique) and bee.authoritative_for (no two concepts claim the same subject) — NOT on one-bee.area-per-directory. A generated index.md carries no frontmatter so it is never the area concept
rationale: D28's form was unimplementable: four of the five concepts in an area had no legal type under the nine-type vocabulary, and the index could not be the area concept because OKF forbids frontmatter in a non-root index.md. Authority belongs to a subject, not a directory

decision: okf-foundation D32 (refines D19): ids are NEVER computed from an arbitrary file path; instead the path segments areas/<slug>/ and work/<id>/ are DERIVED FROM the id. The migrator sets timestamp from the source's last git commit, carries tags from existing frontmatter where present, and sets resource only for a genuinely external asset
rationale: D19's wording asserted the opposite direction and was contradicted simultaneously by D17 (work/<id>/), D27 (--work <id> resolution) and D31 (area id is the slug); and D19 omitted type, the one field OKF marks REQUIRED

decision: okf-foundation D33: frontmatter carry-over is explicit — area->bee.areas, decisions->bee.decisions, sources+parity_sources+parity_decisions->bee.sources, updated->timestamp; coverage is DROPPED (grep confirms no code reads it)
rationale: workflow-state.md carries seven frontmatter keys, not the five previously enumerated, and sources is a multi-thousand-character provenance blob. Without a named target for each key, the carry-across instruction is unexecutable on the very files it governs

decision: okf-foundation D34 (supersedes D22's ships enumeration): ships the profile spec, knowledge.mjs + template mirror, check|index|list|context, the migrator, the docs/knowledge skeleton, advisor-protocol migrated end-to-end with stub and anchor map, THIS FEATURE'S OWN WORK ITEM at work/okf-foundation/, critical-patterns.md migrated into patterns/, the work-item/plan/delivery templates, knowledge check + index --check in the verify chain, and mandatory guard propagation
rationale: Round 2 found context shipping with no <id> that resolves and no critical pattern to include — a consumer with no data is exactly the directory rename D22 exists to avoid. Guard propagation is not optional: a new .bee/bin/lib/knowledge.mjs FAILS scripts/ledger_parity.mjs as an unrecorded managed file until a self-onboard refreshes onboarding.json; a new command group propagates through command-registry into release_manifest --check and both plugin renders; and bee-session-close's mtime scan over docs/specs will fire every session once knowledge moves

decision: okf-foundation D35: every migration emits a COVERAGE REPORT proving each numbered behavior, rule, edge case and pointer bullet in the source lands in exactly ONE concept — no loss, no duplication — asserted by the verify chain
rationale: This is what makes re-authoring a BA spec safe rather than hopeful, and it is the mechanism that lets F2 attack 1464 lines with evidence instead of care. The B1-B36 / R1-R55 numbering makes the invariant machine-checkable

decision: okf-foundation D36 (supersedes D26): implement-plan.md's retirement is DECLARED in the profile in F1 and EXECUTED in F2 when bee-briefing is rewired. Its review state (Draft -> Ready for Review -> Approved -> Needs Revision -> Shipped) moves into plan.md as bee.review_status; the brief renders from it
rationale: The brief is self-declared a projection, but it is ALSO the carrier of real gate-mirroring state and the surface approval happens on (bee-briefing SKILL.md:82-83). Retiring the committed file without naming a home for that state would silently drop it. Declaring in F1 and executing in F2 keeps the declaration honest while skill rewiring stays deferred

decision: okf-foundation D37: a pointer stub carries an ANCHOR MAP — every numbered anchor the source exposed (B17, R26, ...) mapped to the concept path that now owns it — and citations into the migrated file are rewired in the same cell as the stub
rationale: Verified gap: reading-map.md:101-102 cites workflow-state.md B17/B18, R26/R27 and B33, R51. A path-only stub preserves the path and destroys the anchors, leaving silent dangling citations — the exact failure this feature exists to eliminate

decision: auto-approved Gate 1 (total bypass): okf-foundation CONTEXT.md locked after two fresh-eyes review loops — 12 decisions superseded, 20 active, both review verdicts' blockers closed
rationale: gate_bypass_level=total; the human lifted every stop. Recorded rather than asked, per the bypass contract

decision: okf-foundation D38 (owner directive 2026-07-22): the delivered solution must CLOSE THE LEARNING LOOP, not stop at the format layer — documents that sit there are not knowledge. The program ships, in order: format+consumer (S1-S5), then the startup bridge (session start runs knowledge context when a work item exists) and knowledge promote v1 (post-work distillation into concepts) BEFORE wide area migration. Loop closure over coverage: a closed loop on a small store beats a full store with an open loop
rationale: Owner: 'tôi không muốn document chỉ để đó, nó phải là knowledge, giúp càng làm càng hiểu dự án càng tốt lên'. This inverts the F2 default order (migration first) that the integration review already flagged as the weaker choice

decision: auto-approved Gate 2 (total bypass): okf-foundation plan.md frozen — high-risk, 7 slices (S1 format core ... S7 promote v1 per D38), current slice S1 only. Self-onboard rides okf-1 so the chain is never red between cells
rationale: gate_bypass_level=total; recorded, not asked, per the bypass contract

decision: okf-foundation S1 validation: panel NOT READY (narrow return) repaired in place — plugin-render propagation + full generated-file sweep folded into okf-1 as one atomic cell (split rejected: intermediate commit red on test_plugin_distribution drift-pin, v1.9.0 incident class); plan.md S1 file order revised post-validation and Gate 2 re-approved under total bypass; verdict READY WITH CONSTRAINTS
rationale: Panel evidence: test_plugin_distribution.mjs:317-329 byte-pins committed render trees; onboard_bee listTemplateLibModules auto-records new lib modules. Constraints in reports/validation-s1.md

decision: okf-foundation S1 SHIPPED (okf-1 commit 0980904, okf-2 commit da5fa0d): bee knowledge check live — zero-dep emitter-first frontmatter codec with typed failures + round-trip guard, D4 two-level report, D13 JSON/exit contract, D23 bundle confinement; docs/knowledge/ skeleton seeded (root index okf_version-only, log.md ISO entries); Bee OKF Profile documented as docs/specs/okf-profile.md; 61-suite chain green at both cell caps, semantic judge PASS 8/8 on okf-1
rationale: S1 exit state met per plan.md; spec sync obligation for okf-1's behavior change satisfied by the okf-profile area spec shipped in okf-2 (recorded via state scribing-run)

decision: okf-foundation S4 closed (okf-5 a0ea0cc, okf-6 b0d495d): the migration loop is PROVEN end-to-end on real data — advisor-protocol 26/26 anchors owned 0 lost, critical-patterns 47/47, bundle at 53 concepts, chain at 65 suites with 4 knowledge gates. Cell-scoping lesson recorded: okf-6 edited scripts/run_verify.mjs undeclared (a 5-line additive EXTRA_SUITES entry, orchestrator-reviewed and legitimate) — ANY cell that adds a chain gate must declare the chain files in its files list
rationale: Coverage counts prove ownership; the semantic judge separately proved FIDELITY by sampling B3/R9/E5/P2 against the pre-migration blob. The undeclared edit was necessary work with a wrong declaration, not wrong work — recording it so S6/S7 cells declare chain files up front

decision: okf-foundation scribing: the LEARNING LOOP was closed by dogfooding itself — bee knowledge promote proposed the delivery draft, the orchestrator reviewed and applied it as docs/knowledge/work/okf-foundation/delivery.md (bundle 53->54 concepts, check still 0/0). Spec gap found and fixed in the same pass: okf-profile.md documented check and promote but NOT context, index, list, or the startup bridge — added B6 (manifest never content, prefix cut, bytes/4 named as an estimate), B7 (preamble carries the pointer not the payload; silence when absent; phase not feature decides), B8 (anchor coverage gates migration, with the frozen-inventory limit stated)
rationale: A behavior_change that ships without its spec is exactly the drift this feature exists to end; finding it during our own scribing pass is the mechanism working. Applying promote's own draft is the first real proof that the loop produces usable knowledge rather than plausible-looking prose

decision: okf-foundation compounding: 2 critical patterns promoted AS BUNDLE CONCEPTS (surface-structure planning gets fresh-eyed before scope locks; a coverage gate derives its ground truth, never compares two hand-authored lists) — the first time compounding wrote into docs/knowledge/patterns/ instead of prose. The round-trip guard then caught the ORCHESTRATOR's own hand-written frontmatter as not_canonical twice (key order, then quoting), which is exactly the failure class the advisor predicted for hand-edited concepts
rationale: Proof the guard protects against its own authors, not just workers. Also surfaced a real gap: check names the fix ('normalize by re-emitting') but no verb performs it — filed P2 for bee knowledge normalize

decision: okf-migration-f2 Gates 1+2 auto-approved (total bypass): migrate the remaining 10 areas into the bundle, 5 slices, one area per cell ascending by size, workflow-state last against its pre-locked D30 map. F1 fixes the coverage gate to derive ground truth from a git-pinned blob BEFORE any new area migrates
rationale: This repo's own promoted pattern says a gate comparing two hand-authored lists proves consistency not coverage; hand-authoring 10 more registries would multiply that defect tenfold

decision: okf-migration-f2 F8 (supersedes F1): the coverage extractor is shape-aware and self-reporting, and the pin is content-addressed — {commit, path, blob_sha, expected_counts}, ALL asserted, with a count MISMATCH (not just an empty set) a loud typed failure; the inventory reports unparsed lines; each area declares its anchor scheme; the pre-migration source is committed verbatim under docs/history/okf-migration-f2/sources/ and verified with git hash-object so shallow clones still work
rationale: Advisor measured it: onboarding's 22 '- **R1** —' rules inventory as R0 and its behaviors as B0; decision-memory and worktree-parallelism yield 0 anchors. F1's oracle passed by construction because advisor-protocol is the file the regexes were written against. A derived set is trusted MORE than the hand list it replaces, so format-blindness converts lost content into content that never existed

decision: okf-migration-f2 F9 (supersedes F2): migration order is by spec SHAPE, not line count — prove the derived loop on a genuine nine-section area (doctrine-layer, 20 anchors) first; shapeless areas (decision-memory, worktree-parallelism, or any whose inventory reports 0 or heavy unparsed lines) get an explicit per-area anchor scheme at authoring time, the PAT* precedent as model, never a forced fit into B*/R*
rationale: Ascending-by-size put the two unparseable areas first, so the first cell would hit a hard stop instead of cheaply proving the loop — the stated benefit inverted. Shape is the variable that decides whether the mechanism applies at all

decision: okf-migration-f2 F10 (supersedes F3): workflow-state is split across multiple cells grouped by the D30 concept clusters, never one commit
rationale: 139 anchors (B36/R58/E25/P20) is 3-5x either shipped precedent; one commit at the end of a long serial run is peak drift and minimum reviewability

decision: okf-migration-f2 F11: per-anchor fidelity floor — each anchor's owning concept must retain >=60% normalized token overlap with that anchor's text in the pinned blob; below the floor fails the coverage gate naming the anchor
rationale: Set-equality catches LOSS but not anchor-shaped compliance — hitting the count by summarizing an anchor away, which is the degradation mode of a long serial re-authoring run and is mechanically checkable without a judge

decision: okf-migration-f2 F12: per-cell drift telemetry — anchors-per-concept and concepts-per-100-source-lines reported per area, failing on an outlier vs the running median; whole-bundle invariants (authority uniqueness, zero not_canonical, index freshness) run every cell
rationale: Drift should land as a chain red at cell 4, not be discovered at cell 10

decision: auto-approved Gate 2 (bypass): okf-migration-f2 plan revision 2 — honest gate first (F8), order by shape not size (F9), fidelity floor (F11) + drift telemetry (F12), workflow-state split (F10); current slice S1 = f2-1b only
rationale: gate_bypass_level=total. Revision 1 was revoked pre-execution because the advisor consult falsified its premise with measured evidence; rev 2 is the corrected shape

decision: okf-migration-f2: f2-3 BLOCKED correctly and exposed a systemic finding — the ba-nine-section classifier requires bare anchor ids, but 5 remaining areas write rules as '- **R1** —' (onboarding 28, doctrine-layer 17, feedback-digest 15, performance-log 11, decision-memory 9), all deriving R0. decision-memory was classified 'shapeless' by the F9 planning sweep and slated for a special scheme — it is NOT shapeless, its rules were invisible. THE SHAPELESS VERDICT WAS ITSELF AN ARTIFACT OF THE BLINDNESS, so the migration order is re-derived after widening (cell f2-4)
rationale: Had f2-3 proceeded, the coverage gate would have gone GREEN while 17 doctrine-layer business rules (incl. R6 unblocked-is-not-approved and R13-R17 lane ceremony) sat outside the ground truth — lost content reading as content that never existed, the exact defect F8 exists to prevent. The worker refusing to force a scheme is the prohibition working

decision: okf-migration-f2 f2-3 judged NEEDS_REVISION despite a sound migration (39/39, fidelity 1.000 verbatim, chain green): two DISCIPLINE failures — the commit body claimed both anchor readers share AREA_ANCHOR_PATTERN when only one does, and F7s rewire deferral for 7 citations was recorded only in the cell trace where no machine can see it. The judge-record CLI refused a PASS verdict carrying FAIL checks, which is what forced the honest verdict
rationale: A migration can be correct while the record of it is not. Remediation: the deferral is now a P2 backlog row so F3 cannot delete stubs blindly; the regex sharing rides the next migration cell. Recording PASS here would have made every later verdict worth less

decision: okf F13 (closes a gap in D36): implement-plan.md may NOT be retired until its two AUTHORED sections have a named home. Technical Design and Rollback Plan become REQUIRED sections of the bee.plan concept (standard/high-risk lanes) before the retirement executes in F3. D36 relocated only the review state (bee.review_status); these two carry original content authored nowhere else — Technical Design is the narrative of how the pieces fit (distinct from plan.md's Approach, which is which path was chosen), and Rollback is the only rollback discipline bee has anywhere
rationale: Owner asked whether dropping the brief weakens the agent. Measured answer: it does not — 21 cells executed across okf-foundation and okf-migration-f2, exactly 1 references implement-plan.md; workers read CONTEXT.md, plan.md, the source, and the cell. But 9 of the brief's 11 sections are projections while 2 are original content with no other home. Retiring it as written would silently lose them — the exact class of loss this whole programme exists to prevent

decision: okf F14: bee knowledge context must RANK critical patterns by relevance to the work item (tag/area overlap) and cut at budget, instead of D27's include-every-critical rule. Measured defect on first real use: 40 of 45 manifest entries were critical patterns consuming 13000 of 19726 tokens, most unrelated to the task, with 7 further patterns truncated — so an irrelevant pattern can evict a relevant one
rationale: D27's rule was authored when 3 critical patterns existed; the bundle now holds 47 and the rule inverts its own purpose — the consumer built to stop context waste became the largest source of it. Found only by using the tool on real work; no fixture test could catch it because fixtures carry 1-2 patterns

decision: okf-migration-f2 scribing: okf-profile.md gains B9-B12 documenting the gate mechanisms F2 built — content-addressed pins with 8 typed refusals (empty-extraction checked BEFORE counts so 0/0 cannot launder green), mandatory unparsed-block reporting with three schemes and ids read-never-invented, the lexical fidelity floor with its measured discrimination table and its stated terminology limit, and scheme-keyed drift telemetry
rationale: F2 shipped five new verification mechanisms; a spec that documents only check and promote would leave the machinery that actually protects 476 anchors undescribed. The known limits are stated in the spec deliberately — a gate believed inviolable is more dangerous than no gate

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G1: bundle-first WITH FALLBACK — every rewired skill checks for docs/knowledge/ first and, when absent (an un-migrated host repo), falls back to today's docs/specs/ path UNCHANGED, with no deprecation nag
rationale: Owner requirement: old projects keep working. bee ships to other repos that have no bundle; a switchover that only works in bee's own checkout would break every host on the next release

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G2: docs/specs/ becomes read-only for NEW content, enforced by a chain check that fails when a file there is neither a pointer stub nor reading-map.md nor okf-profile.md. Existing stubs are never touched or deleted. Inert in a host repo with no bundle
rationale: Prose alone rots — bee-scribing referenced docs/specs 8 times and docs/knowledge 0 while the bundle already held 116 concepts. Only a guard makes read-only true

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G3: bee-scribing AUTHORS CONCEPTS — updates the owning concept for a known subject, adds a concept for a new subject in an existing area, creates areas/<slug>/ with an overview concept for a new area; frontmatter always through the canonical emitter, never hand-written
rationale: This is the switch; everything else in the OKF programme was preparation. Hand-written frontmatter was caught not_canonical three times this programme, twice by the orchestrator itself

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G4: the reading order becomes bundle -> decisions -> history; bee-hive Session Scout and bee-planning bootstrap read docs/knowledge/ first and name docs/specs/ only as the compatibility surface
rationale: An agent told to read the spec before the code must be sent to where the spec now lives

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G5 (supersedes D27's include-every-critical rule): context RANKS critical patterns by relevance (tag/area overlap with the work item) and cuts at budget, with a small guaranteed floor so a universal lesson is never evicted
rationale: Measured on first real use: 40 of 45 entries were critical patterns taking 13000 of 19726 tokens, mostly irrelevant, with 7 truncated — an irrelevant pattern could evict a relevant one

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G6: okf-profile.md migrates into the bundle it describes, via the same loop and gate as every other area, leaving a pointer stub. G7: stubs are NEVER deleted in this feature — seven live citations resolve through them
rationale: The spec defining the bundle sitting outside it is the last piece of the old model pretending to be current truth; and a stub deleted before its readers move is a silently broken doc

decision: auto-approved Gate 2 (bypass): okf-switchover-f3 — 4 slices, read half fixed before write half flipped, then the old tree fenced, then the profile moved; current slice S1 only
rationale: gate_bypass_level=total. Read-before-write is deliberate: flipping scribing while context still spends two thirds of its budget on noise would close the loop on an untrustworthy consumer and contaminate every later judgement about whether the bundle helps

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G8 (hardens G1): 'has a bundle' becomes ONE exported predicate bundleMode(root), false unless at least one concept actually parses — never a bare path.join and never re-invented in prose per skill. A permanent chain suite drives the scribing decision tree in a bundle-LESS fixture repo
rationale: Advisor measured it: bundleDir is a bare path.join with no existence semantics, and no conformance/render/verify script references either tree, so the fallback would be unasserted prose. A host repo where a stray .gitkeep creates docs/knowledge/ flips to bundle mode with an EMPTY bundle — scribing writes concepts nobody reads while docs/specs quietly stops updating. Bee's own checkout can never exercise the fallback, so only a fixture suite can

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G9 (hardens G3): concept authoring is GATED ON SUBJECT OWNERSHIP via bee.authoritative_for (already used 63x in the bundle) — a new concept may not claim a subject an existing concept owns; and the nine-section skeleton plus the rebuild bar are ported into the area-concept template
rationale: Today's spec quality comes from structure not diligence: one-area-one-file-forever and no-second-spec. G3's new-concept-per-subject removes that mechanism — two concepts on one subject both parse and both index, the exact -v2 failure the scribing skill bans. And the profile grades only frontmatter canonicality, so format-green would read as quality-green

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G10 (supersedes the plan's S1 exit-state wording): the relevance ranking's acceptance is DISCRIMINATION, not survival — a hand-labelled relevant/irrelevant pattern set with non-tied scores, plus a mandatory zero_signal_count that fails the run when too many patterns score zero. The plan's stated oracle ('the 5 relevant entries survive') is REJECTED: those five are the work item, its plan and required_context at ranks 1-3, and the cut is a prefix cut, so the test passes even if every pattern were dropped
rationale: Measured: the work item carries no bee.areas, only 2 of 50 patterns carry any, and tag overlap hits 1 of 50 — 49 tie at zero and the ranking would be a path sort wearing a relevance label. This is F2 learning recommendation 2 recurring verbatim: an oracle whose subject is the fixture it was written against proves nothing

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G11: context emits every EXCLUDED critical pattern as {path, score, reason} and asserts conservation — entries + truncated + excluded == all criticals — failing when zero-score patterns exceed a pinned threshold
rationale: Advisor: G5 converts a LOUD failure (13k tokens of visible noise) into a SILENT one — a pattern that would have prevented a bug is simply absent, and once cut before truncation it is not even named in truncated. Conservation plus an audit line per pattern makes misranking loud instead of invisible

decision: okf-switchover-f3: read-half-first ordering KEPT, but S2 (bee-scribing authors concepts) is explicitly NON-DROPPABLE — the feature may not close on S1+S3. G3 is the switch itself and sits third of four; if the ranking experiment eats the budget, the feature would ship as a manifest tweak and the 8-vs-0 scribing drift would survive another release
rationale: Advisor's counter-argument accepted in part: the contamination premise is weaker than the plan claimed (ranking moves only ranks 4-5 while bundle usefulness is judged on ranks 1-3), but S1 is one cell, so the ordering cost is small and the sequencing benefit is real

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G12: bind the USE of the bundle, not just its content. When the active feature has a bee.work-item concept, cells add REFUSES a cell whose read_first is not derivable from that work item's context manifest, unless the cell declares an explicit context_deviation naming why. Converts an unenforceable question (did the agent read the right thing?) into a checkable one (where did this cell's context come from?)
rationale: Measured split today: 15 mechanical guards protect the bundle's CONTENT (knowledge check, index --check, 11 coverage gates, 2 suites) but ZERO enforce its USE — the session preamble is a pointer an agent may ignore, and the orchestrator itself ignored it for hours across 21 cells with hand-written read_first, using it once only after the owner insisted; that single real use immediately exposed the P1 relevance defect. Owner question: is this hard-bound or a verbal contract. Content is bound; use is not

decision: okf-switchover-f3 f3-2 judged NEEDS_REVISION (8 PASS / 2 FAIL) — recorded by hand because cells judge-record cannot write a NEEDS_REVISION verdict in a taxonomy repo (P1 filed). FAIL 1 anti-fork: the gate is defeated by trailing punctuation, a Cyrillic homoglyph, a non-string authoritative_for, and an empty/null subject (which skips the gate entirely and routes to overview.md even with intent new-concept); two pre-existing owners of one subject resolve to the first by walk order with no detection, and the cited backstop duplicate_authoritative_for is a profile WARNING that the chain never promotes to an error. FAIL 2 product-root: scribingTarget joins docs/specs off root and bundleMode off bundleDir(root) while inject.mjs, backlog.mjs and bee-session-close.mjs all route through resolveProductRoot — in the supported repo-divorce topology a migrated host can be graded bundle-less with its fallback pointing at an empty workshop docs/specs
rationale: The predicate, the fallback purity and the fixture suite survived adversarial probing; the anti-fork gate did not. My own verification only tried case and whitespace variants — normalizeSubject handles those — so I reported the gate as closed. The judge went further and broke it four ways. Recording the failure verbatim so the fix is scoped from evidence, not from my summary of it

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G13 (the authority call the judge asked for): docs/knowledge/ IS a product-doc tree exactly like docs/specs/, so bundleMode and scribingTarget MUST resolve both through resolveProductRoot — the same path inject.mjs, backlog.mjs and bee-session-close.mjs already use. A fixture in the repo-divorce topology (config product_root) is required, because all three existing fixtures are single-root and cannot see this class
rationale: Judge finding: scribingTarget joins docs/specs off root and bundleMode off bundleDir(root). In the supported divorced topology a migrated host would be graded bundle-less and its fallback would point at the empty workshop docs/specs — the exact silent-rot class this cell exists to prevent. state.mjs already declares docs/specs a product tree; the bundle is the same kind of thing and must not be resolved differently

decision: okf-switchover-f3 G14: the anti-fork gate gets three layers, because exact-normalized string matching on free text can never be sufficient. (1) HARDEN the match: NFKC-normalize, strip trailing punctuation, collapse internal whitespace. (2) FAIL CLOSED on malformed input: a non-string authoritative_for is a validation ERROR not a silent skip; an empty/whitespace/null subject with intent new-concept is REFUSED, never routed to overview.md. (3) MAKE THE BACKSTOP BITE: duplicate_authoritative_for is promoted from a profile warning to a chain-failing finding, since layer 1 can never catch a genuine paraphrase
rationale: Judge defeated the shipped gate four ways: trailing period, Cyrillic homoglyph, array-valued claim, and empty subject; and two pre-existing owners resolve to the first by walk order with no detection. No normalization catches paraphrase, so a gate on free text MUST have a real second layer — and the cited one never blocks because the chain runs check without --strict

decision: A cap-time verify EXPIRES the moment anything else is edited. A cell's recorded verify is evidence about the tree as it stood at that cap, never a session-level guarantee: any later edit — including one made outside a tracked cell, and including a one-line citation rewire — obliges a fresh full-chain run before the session ends. okf-switchover-f3's close-out proved the cost: an inject.mjs citation edit after f3-5's green cap left four standing mandatory suites red (lib-mirror parity, release manifest, plugin distribution, preamble contract) plus a stale managed-hash ledger, and the next session opened on a red baseline and paid the repair.
rationale: Every one of those four checks was ALREADY a mandatory suite in the chain; nothing needed building. The failure was purely that the chain was never re-run after the last edit, because the cell's own cap-time green was mistaken for a statement about the session's final tree. This is the fourth recurrence of the derived-artifact class (pattern 20260715), and it also revealed the set is now FOUR deep for one templates/lib touch: mirror copy, plugin tree render, manifest write, self-onboard for the onboarding managed-hash ledger.
alternatives: Rely on the per-cell verify alone (rejected — it is exactly what failed); mechanize by deriving the regen checks into the verify of any cell whose files hit lib/ or rendered trees (still the recorded fix direction, filed as friction, not yet shipped)

decision: A by-name exception in a guard that exists only to cover an interval is DELETED when the interval ends, never relabelled — and both directions are then asserted in the guard's selftest (the real artifact passes structurally; the same filename WITHOUT its structural marker fails). Applied in okf-switchover-f3 f3-5: okf-profile.md left the fence's NAMED_EXCEPTIONS set entirely rather than being re-pointed at the 'stub' verdict.
rationale: Relabelling preserves a name-based pass that keeps saying yes if the artifact's structural marker is ever dropped or its frontmatter ever breaks — reintroducing under a new label exactly the silent rot the structural branch exists to close. A named exception that outlives its interval is a standing permission for that filename to hold anything at all. The general form: filename allowlists rot the first time something is added or renamed, and a rotted allowlist stops guarding SILENTLY.
alternatives: Relabel the exception from 'profile' to 'stub' (rejected — keeps the name-based pass alive with no expiry); leave it untouched (rejected — same hole, plus now misleading)

decision: okf-integration-close-f4 Gate 1 auto-approved under gate_bypass=total: CONTEXT.md locks D1-D9 closing the seven edge gaps the post-f3 audit found (preamble digest + project map still old-model, the two bee-hive reference files carrying zero bundle mentions, grooming blind to bundle rot, planning's tiny/small bootstrap, compounding's ownership prose, and the derived-artifact discipline for the whole feature).
rationale: Total autopilot is on; the human has removed every stop. Scope was locked by a mechanical audit with file:line anchors and two gaps confirmed by direct observation of this session's own preamble, so there are no gray areas for exploring to resolve.

decision: okf-integration-close-f4 Gates 1-3 auto-approved under gate_bypass=total. Shape: three cells — f4-1 the two bee-hive reference files (measured 0 bundle mentions in the files SKILL.md defers to), f4-2 the grooming/planning/compounding prose corrections, f4-3 the session preamble behavior change (digest + project map + nudge) which also owns the four derived-artifact regens for the whole feature per D9.
rationale: Total autopilot is on and the human has removed every stop. Scope came from a mechanical audit with file:line anchors, two of its findings confirmed by direct observation of a live session preamble; feasibility is not in question because every gap is a named passage in a named file plus one lib function with existing test coverage.

decision: okf-integration-close-f4 D1 refinement: in bundle mode the preamble's critical-patterns digest states the TOTAL count and lists the N MOST RECENT rows from the bundle index's '## Critical patterns' section, plus the path to the full index. It does not rank.
rationale: Measured: that section carries ~50 rows in DATE order (concept filenames are date-prefixed), so a naive first-N-lines cut would surface the ten oldest lessons forever and never a recent one — swapping one arbitrary cut (the stub's frontmatter) for another. Relevance ranking is knowledge context's job and needs a work item to rank against, which the preamble does not have; newest-first is honest and cheap. Red evidence in docs/history/okf-integration-close-f4/reports/red-preamble-before.md shows 4 of the current digest's 10 lines are YAML delimiters and the other 6 are the stub's redirect prose.
alternatives: First N lines of the section (rejected — permanently oldest); run the relevance ranker (rejected — no work item to rank against at preamble time)

decision: okf-integration-close-f4 adds cell f4-4 beyond the locked D1-D9 scope: run_verify's hermeticity scrub covers CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and BEE_SESSION_ID but misses BEE_AGENT_NAME — the third identity variable, and the one bee's own critical rule 5 mandates on write-heavy commands. Obeying rule 5 and then running the configured verify manufactures a false red in the write-guard suites.
rationale: Reproduced deterministically: without the var 31 passed / 0 failed; with BEE_AGENT_NAME=w-test, 28 passed / 3 failed, every failure being 'the acting session's own hold must never block its own write' — the leaked name becomes the acting agent identity inside checkWrite. It cost this feature twice: two workers reported it as flake, and the orchestrator misdiagnosed it as concurrent-chain-run noise and told the user so. Leaving a known false-red generator in the chain would cost every future session the same misdiagnosis, and the fix is one delete beside two that already exist.
alternatives: Leave it and document the collision in prose (rejected — prose has already failed twice in one feature); forbid the BEE_AGENT_NAME prefix on verify commands (rejected — it inverts the contract, making the harness's leak the author's problem)

decision: A green re-run is evidence about the conditions it ran under, not about the conditions that produced the red. Before accepting ANY environmental explanation for a failing suite — sibling cell in flight, concurrency, flake — reproduce it by toggling exactly ONE variable while holding everything else fixed. If it cannot be made to appear and disappear on demand, it is not diagnosed.
rationale: Learned by walking into it this session. Two workers reported write-guard reds after running the chain concurrently; the orchestrator applied the existing 'a shared-suite red is not yours while a sibling is in flight' pattern, re-ran serially, saw green, concluded sibling noise, and stated that to the user. The real cause was BEE_AGENT_NAME leaking into spawned suites; the serial re-run was green only because it happened not to carry the prefix. The heuristic supplies a plausible story on demand, and a plausible story is what stops an investigation — most dangerously when the failing assertions are coordination guards, where that story is always available.
alternatives: Trust the existing shared-suite heuristic as-is (rejected — it is what produced the wrong answer); treat all such reds as real and investigate every one fully (rejected — the heuristic is usually right, which is exactly why it needs a precondition rather than deletion)

decision: Before changing any guard that has gone red, state which of two acts you are performing — loosening what it takes to pass, or correcting what is measured — and PROVE it with a negative control that constructs the failure the guard exists to catch and shows it still fires. Without the control the two are indistinguishable, including in the diff and the commit message.
rationale: f4-7: a drift metric went red on an area whose coverage was perfect; it had merely grown concepts that can never own a historical anchor. Four one-line edits (widen the band, lower min-samples, exclude the area, edit the pin) would each have cleared it and destroyed the signal. The negative control did more than certify the denominator fix — it proved the OLD metric was already blind: an area with every anchor dumped into one concept scored comfortably in band, because empty sibling files diluted the file-count denominator. Secondary signal, useful but not sufficient: a corrected measurement tends to tighten the population, a loosened threshold always widens it.
alternatives: Trust the author's stated intent (rejected — intent is what a worker optimizing for green will always report); forbid touching guards that go red (rejected — this guard was genuinely wrong and needed fixing)

decision: A cell's must-haves state the PROPERTY wanted, never the observation the orchestrator predicts — and a must-have contradicted by measurement is reported back, never satisfied.
rationale: f4-7's cell asserted 'every OTHER pinned area's row is UNCHANGED', written on the orchestrator's confident but false assumption that at migration time every concept owned anchors. Five areas already carried an authored overview concept owning none, so six rows moved. The worker measured it and reported the correction instead of trimming the fix; had it complied, the fix would have needed to special-case five areas — hidden complexity that later reads as inexplicable. The property actually wanted was 'no area's row moves out of band and no threshold moves', which survived contact with the repo where the prediction did not.

decision: The scope of a census/fence/audit is derived by MEASUREMENT before the check is trusted: run the unrestricted search first, inspect what returns, then narrow — with every exclusion carrying its reason in the code. A check whose scope was never measured proves nothing when it passes.
rationale: Three misses in one session, same author, same shape, each reporting CLEAN: an instruction-surface audit whose grep omitted hooks/ (where the P1 was), a tagless-caller census scoped to lib/** that passed green while a sibling file carried a live instance, and a first audit that read for meaning where grep -c found two more files instantly. A too-narrow scope does not fail loudly — it returns the most reassuring output a check can produce, and everyone downstream inherits the assumption. Review attention goes to the rule because that is where thinking visibly happened; the scope is typed once from memory.
alternatives: Review the rule harder (rejected — the rules were all correct; the scopes were not); always scan repo-wide with no exclusions (rejected — legitimate exclusions exist, e.g. a fixture whose violation is its subject matter; the fix is that each exclusion states its reason in code)

decision: A cross-cutting write-time refusal is unfinished until the callers already in the tree are swept in the same change, with a source-derived check left behind. The check must never flag a caller that legitimately forwards a user-supplied value, and must be proven by injecting a violation.
rationale: The untagged-decision refusal shipped tested against the caller it was written for; five internal callers already in the tree passed no tags and were all live. Three unwound their operation; one sat in a best-effort catch and silently dropped its audit line; the fifth writes after the state lock releases on feature close, so a throw leaves the feature closed with its state mutated and the waiver's justification absent. The visible symptom months later was a rework verdict that could not be recorded and had to be hand-written. New-rule work is forward-looking by nature — existing callers are invisible because they are not part of the change.

decision: A flag the caller passed is either honoured or explained — never silently dropped. And a guard that directs writes to a location obliges the reclaimer to reach that same location.
rationale: issues-46-53 surfaced both as live defects. --cleanup was accepted and evaporated on the no-op merge path, exit 0, no message; the rule it followed ('strictly post-commit') had conflated the real safety property ('nothing would be lost') with a proxy ('a commit happened'). Separately the write guard refuses scratch-shaped writes elsewhere and names the scratch ROOT as the place to write, while the sweeper's inventory saw only directories — so 58 of 76 entries were unreachable by every flag including the one documented as clearing the lot. Both were invisible because each half looked correct alone.

decision: A conditional rule must not be rendered inside an unconditional list — state the trigger FIRST and place the rule where its trigger lives. Cost complaints about a harness are measured before they are believed: check what actually executes, then what the instructions demand.
rationale: issues-46-53: the baseline gate said 'before claiming any cell' as item 7 of a startup list whose other items said 'every session', so agents ran a 30-90s chain to answer questions touching no cell — reported as 'it runs verify at startup', though nothing executes verify automatically at all. Measuring separated the two: hooks are ~150ms and ~1.4k tokens, while the mandated reading is ~99KB plus a 20k-token budget, with status and decisions re-fetching what the preamble already injected. Three of the seven issues in this batch named a cause that measurement disproved.

decision: herding-adopt D11 CONFIRMED BY OWNER: merge is an owner gesture, not a loop. Bootstrap starts only the dispatch loop; merge runs single-shot on request via the --once flag the contribution already ships.
rationale: The advisor measured that the deferred-reconciliation 'safe failure' does not exist: the lane classifier anchors on the Status VALUE rather than column position, so it already parses this repo's table — which is why an earlier review got 8 of 8 rows through it. Two rows (one installer/release) satisfy every dispatch condition today, and bee-exploring's own rule manufactures more such rows as a side effect of normal operation. Unattended merge alone carries the merge-authority hard-gate flag, the ~91-minute stop-latency window, and the exposure of running verify over code the unsandboxed working agents wrote. Making merge a keystroke drops one of four hard-gate flags outright and costs the owner only presence.
alternatives: Keep both loops with a patched stop gesture, an enable marker and a narrowed allowlist (offered and declined by the owner — merge authority would still rest with automation)

decision: herding-adopt D7-FINAL, OWNER DECISION: the four working agents keep --permission-mode bypassPermissions as an explicitly accepted risk with its blast radius recorded; the two CONTROL panes are narrowed to an enumerated command surface, never to 'read-only'.
rationale: Working agents need broad authority to actually write code — that is what the feature exists to create — and the contribution states this as a deliberate accepted-risk choice. Blast radius recorded plainly: each such agent can reach the whole filesystem, the network and the invoking user's credentials, with steady state up to four concurrent. The control panes are narrowed because a cold model at roughly 2,880 invocations a day will eventually improvise. 'Read-only' was measured WRONG as the narrowing target: dispatch creates a worktree and registers a grant, and merge aborts against main, writes markers and runs a cleanup that deletes a branch — an implementer taking read-only literally would produce a dispatch pane that cannot dispatch and a merge pane that cannot merge, stalling silently every 60 seconds. The halves are also coupled: the merge pane runs verify against the just-merged tree, executing code the working agents authored.

decision: Split automation at the point where an action becomes hard to reverse: automate the recoverable side, keep the irreversible side a human gesture. The test is not 'can this be automated' but 'what does one bad iteration cost' — and when you find yourself adding guards to make an irreversible unattended step acceptable, that is the signal to make it a gesture instead.
rationale: herding-adopt: an external contribution ran dispatch (start work in an isolated worktree, recoverable) and merge (land it in main, irreversible) as two equally-autonomous loops. Every serious risk concentrated in merge — unattended merge authority, a ~91-minute stop-latency window, and running verify over unsandboxed agent code. Demoting merge to a single-shot owner gesture dropped one of four hard-gate flags outright and shrank stop-latency to the harmless half. Its three 'containments' were each an LLM counting panes / reading one backlog line / a once-per-cycle stop check — guards doing a present human's job, worse.

decision: A claim about how existing code behaves — a contribution's or your own plan's — is a measurement, not a premise. Run it before trusting it, and run the claims the work leans on hardest first.
rationale: herding-adopt: the contribution's docs named containments (lane filter, slot cap, stop gesture, 'will not pick up hard-gate work') that all measured weaker than stated — the lane filter passed 8 of 8 real rows including 'delete the JS runtime'. And my OWN plan asserted the control panes 'never need to write' (false — they create worktrees and clean) and that a backlog-format mismatch made the loop select nothing (false — the classifier anchors on the status value and already parsed the repo, two rows qualified that moment). The advisor caught both of mine by running them. Documentation and plans describe intent; only execution describes behavior.

decision: compaction-hardening D14: bee ships NO provider-native compaction transport adapter — no OpenAI Responses compaction_trigger, no previous_response_id continuation, no opaque-artifact replay, no compaction-provider interface.
rationale: bee does not own the transport; Claude Code and Codex each own their own compaction. The evidence usually cited for native transport is a task-continuation gap (35.6 percent vs 100 percent in the referenced benchmark) — and task state is exactly what already lives on disk in .bee/, so bee recovers it deterministically at zero provider coupling. Native artifacts are opaque, model-specific and unauditable, which disqualifies them as a source of truth for a workflow. Revisit only if bee ever owns an outer runner.

decision: compaction-hardening D1/D2: the guardrails doctrine text is authored in skills/bee-hive/templates/AGENTS.block.md and propagated to all four rendered projections plus root AGENTS.md; its replacement wording must state exactly three things — both runtimes ship hooks from one shared catalog, the enforcement floor is the shared helpers, and Codex hook EXECUTION is unverified so self-honoring remains the fallback on any runtime whose hook execution is unconfirmed.
rationale: The sentence 'on Codex you must honor them yourself' is read by every session on both runtimes and is the measured source of the recurring 'bee prioritizes Claude Code' reading — .codex/hooks.json ships 8 lifecycle events and is onboarding-tracked. But replacing it with a flat parity claim would be the same defect inverted: docs/06-runtime-integration.md:67 still lists Codex hook discovery as an open question. Editing AGENTS.md alone would be reverted by the next render.

decision: compaction-hardening D3 (helper floor): every behavior this feature adds is reachable through a bee.mjs verb, and each hook only calls that verb's library function — no behavior exists solely inside a hook.
rationale: This is what makes the feature runtime-neutral in fact rather than in prose: if a runtime never executes .codex/hooks.json, the model can still reach every surface by command. It is bee's own stated design — enforcement lives in the shared helpers first, hooks are a second belt (docs/06-runtime-integration.md:8).

decision: compaction-hardening D16 (supersession): the compact-scoped capsule supersedes intent-anchor ia-1's D4/D5 for the compact source ONLY. hooks/test_hook_contracts.mjs:2740-2778 currently asserts the anchor path is strictly additive over the full preamble for both compact and resume; that assertion is split in the same cell that lands the capsule — resume keeps byte-identical additivity, compact asserts the capsule's required items and the absence of the startup-only sections.
rationale: A locked decision encoded in a green test cannot be overridden silently. Without the note a planner either implements the capsule and hits a red verify, or reads the red test as authority and drops the capsule. The fresh-eyes reviewer caught this by running the test, not by reading the plan.

decision: compaction-hardening D17/D18: all code edits land in the source trees (skills/bee-hive/templates/lib/, hooks/), never in the .bee/bin/ projection, which is a byte-identical mirror gated by scripts/test_lib_mirror.mjs:16-20 and refreshed by onboarding; the mirror refresh plus onboarding sha256 update is the feature's final cell, verified by that mirror test going green.
rationale: The first CONTEXT.md draft cited .bee/bin/ paths as the edit target for every code integration point — the exact defect its own D1 rationale exists to prevent, applied to the doctrine prose but not to the other 90 percent of the feature. Editing a mirror produces a change the next onboarding silently reverts, and leaves three managed hook hashes stale.

decision: auto-approved Gate 1 (bypass total): compaction-hardening — CONTEXT.md locked with 18 decisions after two fresh-eyes review loops (4 P1 + 8 P2 + 5 P3 raised, all folded in).
rationale: gate_bypass_level=total; the owner has removed every human checkpoint. The document was independently reviewed twice and every finding verified against the repo before locking; the second loop confirmed all seven claimed fixes and its three remaining P2s were applied.

decision: compaction-hardening escalates standard -> high-risk. Flag count 5: public contracts (docs/07-contracts.md:104 and :216 both document contracts D6 falsifies), cross-platform (must hold on Claude Code and Codex — D3's helper floor exists for exactly that divergence), changes behavior an existing test asserts (D16, hooks/test_hook_contracts.mjs:2740-2780), requires replacing existing proof (the compact half of the additivity assertion is replaced, not kept green alongside a new one), multi-domain (doctrine prose + lib module + three hooks + CLI dispatcher + tests + onboarding hashes). No hard-gate flag is present.
rationale: 4+ flags is high-risk by the mechanical rule; even discounting the public-contracts flag the count stays at 4. Standard was the intake guess before the fresh-eyes reviews surfaced the test-supersession and mirror-coverage findings — the mode gate re-runs upward the moment evidence demands it, and this is that evidence.

decision: auto-approved Gate 2 (bypass total): compaction-hardening high-risk plan — one slice of 6 cells, L1 discovery closed all three deferred questions, two HIGH risk rows handed to validating.
rationale: gate_bypass_level=total covers every lane including high-risk. The shape rests on measured facts: the two-command render path, the confirmed bee.mjs copy_helper source, and PAT37's four-time-recurring derived-artifact chain.

decision: compaction-hardening slice 1 FAILS validation: NOT READY - RETURN TO PLANNING. The root un-owned decision is who renders the intent anchor on source=compact — the hook (which already prefixes it via ANCHOR_LEAD_SOURCES at bee-session-init.mjs:44) or the capsule (D6 item 1). It must be settled before re-shaping, because it decides whether D16's test supersession is needed at all and therefore whether the 'replaces existing proof' mode-gate flag is real.
rationale: Measured, not argued: (1) ch-2 creating compaction.mjs turns release_manifest --check and ledger_parity --check red repo-wide, and neither is in ch-2..ch-5's verify — PAT37's fifth recurrence, in a plan that cites PAT37; (2) test_bee_cli.mjs:2558 asserts EVERY registry entry's example executed, so registering compact-capsule in ch-3 while ch-4 builds it makes the repo red; (3) ch-4 is behavior_change with a verify that passes whether the capsule is correct, empty or throwing; (4) the anchor would render twice on compact; (5) ch-1's derived gate globs AGENTS.block.md and so cannot see the merged root AGENTS.md that D1 names, and its Object.keys derivation yields ['hooks'] not the 8 events; (6) ch-1 runs onboard --apply which writes four other cells' declared files while scheduled in the same wave as ch-2. Baseline itself is green (run_verify exit 0, 63.6s measured — the plan's 30-32s figure was 2x wrong).

decision: compaction-hardening D19 (SUPERSEDES D6 item 1; RETIRES D16): the HOOK keeps owning the intent anchor on source=compact, exactly as it does today via intentLeadBlock/ANCHOR_LEAD_SOURCES. The capsule is the preamble REPLACEMENT only — items 2-12 — and it preserves the '- Phase:' label verbatim. D6 item 1 no longer means 'the capsule renders the anchor'; it means 'the anchor still leads, rendered by the hook, unchanged'.
rationale: Measured by the feasibility lens: both fixtures in hooks/test_hook_contracts.mjs:2740-2780 render through the same source=compact path, so under this ownership the control output is itself a capsule and out.endsWith(control) stays green untouched — no test supersession is needed and D16 is unnecessary. Under the opposite ownership the anchor renders twice (bee-session-init.mjs:44 already prefixes it) and both the anchor-first must-have and the replacement assertion still pass on the duplicate, i.e. the split test would not have caught its own defect. Choosing hook ownership removes a double render, retires a HIGH-rated test surgery, and keeps ia-1's shipped contract intact.

decision: compaction-hardening: D19 drops two mode-gate flags — 'changes behavior an existing test asserts' and 'requires replacing existing proof' both evaporate, since no existing assertion changes. Honest count is now 3 (public contracts, cross-platform, multi-domain), which the mechanical rule scores as STANDARD. The lane is nevertheless KEPT at high-risk as a deliberate over-protection, not as a claim that the count still says 4.
rationale: The change sits in the orientation path every session on both runtimes depends on, and this slice already failed one validation pass on six blocking findings. Recording the honest count separately from the retained lane keeps the mode gate trustworthy: a padded count would corrupt the rule for every future feature, while a deliberately retained lane is a judgement the reviewer can see and contest.

decision: auto-approved Gate 2 (bypass total): compaction-hardening plan revision 2 — 8 cells, strictly serial, every lib-touching cell owns its own manifest+ledger regen, the hook keeps anchor ownership, and the doctrine gate derives both counts plus a selftest.
rationale: gate_bypass_level=total. Revision 2 exists because revision 1 failed validation on six blocking findings, each re-measured by the orchestrator before acceptance; every one has a named correction (D19-D22) and the previously-open matrix rows now carry measured evidence. Baseline confirmed green at 84 suites / 63.6s.

decision: compaction-hardening D23: the forced PreCompact anchor nudge (D11) DOES change an existing assertion — hooks/test_hook_contracts.mjs:2692-2712 asserts the with-anchor PreCompact message equals the anchor block plus the no-anchor control's exact bytes, and the nudge fires precisely when readIntent is null, i.e. only in the control. decision: rust-port D5 supersession (per-command budget, status): the 5 ms spawn-inclusive p95 target does NOT apply to `queen-bee status --json`. Measured on the pinned host-real fixture (queen-bench --check, 50 runs, spawn-inclusive): warm p95 52.615 ms, cold p95 52.094 ms, node baseline for the same command on the same fixture p95 192.772 ms, queen-bee ping floor p95 2.145 ms. D5's own escape clause fires here ('a proven-unreachable command gets an explicit per-command budget logged as a supersession — never a shrunk fixture'): the fixture was NOT shrunk and the volatile allowlist was NOT widened. Cause is measured, not guessed: 40.5 ms of the run is in-process, 40.1 ms of that inside reader blocks, envelope 0.439 ms — duplicated store I/O inside bee-core (decisions.jsonl 700 KB parsed 4x per run at decisions.rs:55/:120, doubled by recovery.rs:519-523; the 250 cell files scanned 6x; scan_transcript_roots run 2x at recovery.rs:457/:586). Perfect dedup floors at ~13 ms in-process / ~17-20 ms process — still ~4x of 5 ms, and it needs bee-core signature changes outside rust-port-15's file scope. INTERIM BUDGET: 70 ms dev p95 for status (CI perf smoke 210 ms, keeping D5's 3x runner-variance ratio) — a regression guard, never the goal. FOLLOW-UP IS MANDATORY: a dedup cell (per-invocation store-read memoization inside bee-core) targets <=20 ms dev p95, at which point this budget tightens to 25 ms. Status never returns to 5 ms. SECONDARY FINDING qualifying decision a7d7b3d5: cold and warm cache p95 are indistinguishable on this fixture (52.094 vs 52.615 ms), so the review-git cache is NOT what dominates the status path today — store I/O is; a7d7b3d5 stands as written, but its expected ~10 ms warm-vs-cold delta is not observable at this fixture's review-candidate count. D3 byte-compatibility is untouched: bee-parity --status-check is green on all four legs (plain/json 3339 B, plain/text 1549 B, enriched/json 4926 B, enriched/text 2464 B), zero stdout diff, both exits 0, store trees equal, per-leg seeded-mutation controls detected — independently re-run by the orchestrator, exit 0.
rationale: D5 pre-authorized exactly this escape, and the alternatives it names — a shrunk fixture or a widened allowlist — are the dishonest green D5 exists to forbid. 52 ms is still 3.7x faster than the node leg on the same fixture with zero subprocess spawns on the status path, which is D5's real demand; the remaining gap is duplicated I/O with a named cause, a named fix, and a named target.
alternatives: (a) Block the slice until bee-core dedup lands — rejected: the dedup needs bee-core signature changes outside this cell's file scope, and holding a green byte-parity proof hostage to a separate optimization buys nothing. (b) Keep the 5 ms gate red and cap anyway — rejected: capping around a red verify is the false green the cap rules exist to prevent. (c) Shrink the fixture or widen the allowlist to reach 5 ms — refused by D5 in writing.

decision: rust-port house rule for every remaining slice (from Slice 2's four rework rounds): (1) every unit a cell's action names gets an oracle diff against the frozen reference — correct-by-inspection is not a proof; (2) anything under the D3 byte contract is compared as BYTES, with volatile values redacted in the raw text and the redactor failing closed — parsed-value comparison is banned there, because this workspace's serializer configuration makes map equality order-blind and two real key-order breaks hid behind exactly that; (3) a fixture must be shown to REACH the branch its test names, proven by removal (neutralize the seeding, require the failure) — an empty-collection shortcut is the commonest silent substitute, and a table-driven row set where no case carries two competing fields cannot detect a priority-order regression; (4) a harness clears every ambient input it reads, pins its own per scenario identically for both legs, and asserts a positive marker proving the pinned branch was reached; (5) a defect fixed inside a port cell ships with red-first evidence quoted in the cap. Each rule is here because its absence shipped a green proof of something untrue in Slice 2.
rationale: All four Slice-2 rework rounds were triggered by proof gaps, not by wrong ported behaviour: an uncalled reader, an unentered branch, a fixture whose comment overclaimed, and a comparison structurally blind to the contract's own dimension. Encoding the rules as a standing house rule is cheaper than rediscovering each one per slice, and the knowledge bundle's rust-runtime proof-discipline concept carries the long form.
alternatives: Leave it to per-cell must_haves — rejected: Slice 2's must_haves already said 'every ported reader matches its mjs oracle' and a reader with zero callers still shipped, so the rule needs to be a standing check the worker applies, not a sentence in one cell.

decision: queen-bee status per-invocation shared reads: each store is read at ONE instant per invocation; cross-store consistency remains unguaranteed, exactly as today. NOT snapshot semantics.
rationale: rust-port-23 threads a caller-supplied per-invocation memo (bee_core::shared_reads::SharedReads) through the status readers, taking build_status from 4 decisions-journal parses / 6 cells-directory scans / 2 transcript-root scans down to 1 / 1 / 1 (queen-bench D5 fixture; status warm p95 52.6ms -> 26.96ms). Before, the stores were read at roughly eight distinct instants, so a concurrent write mid-invocation could yield an internally inconsistent payload; after, each store is read once per invocation. Decisions, cells and transcript roots are still loaded at DISTINCT moments and a journal read racing an in-flight append is still possible, so cross-store consistency is unchanged and the claim is deliberately not 'snapshot semantics'. status takes no D9 locks, so the lock and lease conformance surface is untouched. The frozen mjs oracle still re-reads, so under concurrent mutation the two runtimes differ; acceptable because nothing can legitimately depend on a torn read, and D3 contracts the stores formats and semantics, not the reference implementation incidental read count. Byte-parity under single-threaded conditions is unchanged: all 6 bee-parity status legs zero-diff with per-leg mutation controls detected.
alternatives: REJECTED: a process-global or lazily-initialized static cache, and an on-disk cache like the review one (these stores change on every write, so the staleness guard that makes the review cache safe does not exist here). REJECTED: a concurrent-mutation differential test against the mjs oracle, which would assert nondeterministic behaviour nobody contracted for and be flaky by construction. REJECTED: an eager shared-read struct, which would have turned chain-nudge scribing_debt feature-gated cells scan into an unconditional one on every SubagentStop hook event with every correctness test still green; the memo is lazy for exactly this reason.

decision: rust-port-24 settles the status budget after the read-dedup (rust-port-23): measured on the pinned host-real fixture with queen-bench --check, spawn-inclusive, warm cache, >=50 runs each. Three independent standard passes (50 runs) gave warm p95 24.737 ms / 25.302 ms / 23.666 ms; a fourth confirmatory pass at 200 runs (tighter percentile estimate) gave 24.467 ms — mean of all four 24.543 ms. This is ABOVE e119fc8b's 20 ms follow-up target: outcome (b), the target is not reached, and the interim 70 ms budget is retired in favor of a budget derived honestly from the measured number rather than an unmet 25 ms promise. HEADROOM RULE applied to the canonical 24.467 ms figure (largest sample, matches the 4-pass mean almost exactly, so not a favorably cherry-picked value): round up to the next 5 ms multiple (25), plus one 5 ms step of headroom = 30 ms. New STATUS_BUDGET_MS = 30 ms dev p95 (queen-bench/src/main.rs), CI perf smoke = 90 ms (D5's 3x runner-variance ratio preserved). ping keeps its own unchanged 5 ms floor (PING_BUDGET_MS; CI 15 ms) — the two budgets are never collapsed into one. Per-block warm profile (queen-bee status --json --profile against the same fixture shape): 19.352 ms in-process, dominated by build_recovery_block/transcripts (9.463 ms, 53.5%), list_cells/counts (4.291 ms, 24.3%), read_backlog_counts (1.767 ms, 10.0%), build_review_block/gix warm (0.678 ms, 3.8%), tier_mix (0.518 ms) and global_scribing_debt (0.465 ms) — everything else <0.3%. Fixture floors and measurement method unchanged from e119fc8b/D5 (D5 escape honored: nothing shrunk, nothing widened).
rationale: e119fc8b named this cell's job explicitly: settle whether the 20 ms target is reachable after the dedup and either confirm the 25 ms budget or log a new one with the profile. The dedup (rust-port-23) took warm p95 from ~52.6 ms to ~24.5 ms — real, large progress — but landed short of 20 ms by roughly 4-5 ms, dominated now by build_recovery_block (transcript scanning) and list_cells, neither eliminable inside this cell's own file scope (crates/queen-bench/*), so the honest record is a superseding decision with a real number, not a silently-kept unmet promise. Alternatives considered: (a) leave e119fc8b's 25 ms target standing unmet — rejected, an unreachable promise left in the record is exactly what this cell exists to correct; (b) round the measured 24.467-25.302 ms range down to fit the 25 ms ceiling — rejected, the headroom rule forbids a budget below the measured number's derived floor and 25 ms would make the gate fail on data close to the run that set it; (c) use the single highest replicate (25.302 ms) as canonical, yielding 35 ms — considered but not chosen, it is an outlier at the edge of the observed range versus the 4-pass mean (24.543 ms) and the larger-sample run (24.467 ms); reported transparently in the cell's report alongside the chosen 30 ms so the choice is checkable.

decision: windows-path-identity wpi-2: a POSIX-only machine CANNOT revert-detect the three canonical-comparison assertions, and that limit is recorded rather than papered over. On POSIX, canonicalPathsEqual(a,b) and a===b agree by construction for these values, so reverting an assertion line to === is a semantic no-op locally and no local test can see it. The goal-check judge called this out and marked it fixability "authority" — needing a decision, not an automatic fix. The orchestrator overrode that and directed a third round adding a second pass per assertion against a win32-rendered value; the worker implemented it faithfully, and the orchestrator then measured that reverting the original assertion STILL passes, because the second pass is a separate line that the revert does not touch. The judge was right and the override was wrong. WHAT THE SECOND PASSES ARE WORTH, and why they stay: they prove the canonical comparison ACCEPTS a win32-rendered value that a bare === REJECTS — that is, they prove the fix does the thing Windows needs, which is the property actually under test. What no local proof can establish is that the assertion lines themselves use the canonical form; that is established by reading them and confirmed by Windows CI. Recorded so no later reader mistakes the absence of a revert-guard for an oversight.
rationale: Three rounds on one cell, the third spent chasing a property that cannot exist on this platform. The honest close is to name the limit, keep the coverage that is real, and stop — rather than a fourth round or a guard that reads as proof while proving something else.
