decision: The readJson parse-error warning text is an ACCEPTED cross-runtime divergence, reconciled by a two-directional shape assertion in the parity normalizer — never by a blanket stderr strip, and never by a per-group deliberate_exceptions line
rationale: packages/bee/lib/fsutil.mjs:42 warns 'bee: could not parse JSON at <file> — <err.message>' where err.message is V8's parser text; crates/bee-core/src/fsutil.rs:82-88 emits the same sentence with serde_json's text. The two can never match, and crates/bee-parity/src/normalize.rs:172-198 correctly refuses any asymmetric stderr strip. Measured blast radius from the rpl-2 goal-check: JSONL reads are UNAFFECTED (readJsonl skips corrupt lines silently on both sides, fsutil.mjs:112-130 / fsutil.rs:139-160), but whole-JSON reads are exposed at reviews.mjs:109,128, feedback.mjs:547,772, decisions.mjs:127 plus state.mjs (11 sites) and cells.mjs (6) which nearly every command transits. Left unsettled, every remaining ledger group would silently omit the unparseable-store shape and the port would ship with zero coverage of corrupt-JSON reads. The resolution follows the precedent rpl-1 set for the '[bee] <cmd> <n>ms' line: a declared artifact whose INVARIANT PREFIX is asserted byte-identical on both legs and whose parser-specific tail is the only part allowed to differ, with the allowance named and shape-checked rather than blanket-ignored. Filed as cell rpl-11 and made a dependency of rpl-3, so it lands before any further group registers.

decision: The readJson parse-failure warning is a DECLARED stderr artifact: its invariant prefix (`bee: could not parse JSON at <path> — `, path included) and invariant suffix (`. Using fallback; fix the file.`) are compared byte-for-byte between the legs, and ONLY the parser tail between them is replaced with <PARSE_ERROR>, and only when it matches the JSON-parser dialect of the runtime that produced it (V8 on the mjs leg, serde_json on the queen-bee leg).
rationale: packages/bee/lib/fsutil.mjs:42 quotes V8's err.message; crates/bee-core/src/fsutil.rs:82-88 quotes serde_json's. Measured side by side over one corrupt store: mjs said "Unexpected token 'o', ...\"seable\": not json at\"... is not valid JSON", queen-bee said "expected ident at line 1 column 26". The two can never match byte-for-byte and D1 freezes the mjs leg, so with no declared allowance every remaining ledger group would have shipped zero coverage of unparseable whole-JSON store reads. The warning is REPLACED, never removed, so a leg that emits none where the other does is still a diff; an empty, prose, or wrong-dialect tail is an error, not a pass.
alternatives: A blanket stderr strip of anything matching the warning (rejected: destroys the very coverage this buys and hides a port that swallowed the parse failure); a per-group deliberate_exceptions line (rejected: pushes the same hole into every group instead of closing it); accepting the tail unconditionally (rejected: the tail is where a wrong-runtime or non-parser message would hide).

decision: COMMIT DISCIPLINE for concurrent workers in one checkout: a worker NEVER runs 'git add' then 'git commit' — the index is shared, so a sibling's commit sweeps up whatever this worker staged (observed live: w2-3's content landed in w2-1's commit b435567d, leaving w2-3 with an empty marker commit). Workers commit path-scoped in one atomic step: git commit -- <path> [<path>...] with the message; nothing is ever staged. Applies to every parallel wave
rationale: first real defect of parallel-by-default; one-commit-per-cell traceability broke without any content loss

decision: PARALLEL GIT SAFETY, two absolute rules for workers sharing a checkout: (1) never 'git add' — commit path-scoped in one step (git commit -- <paths>), because the index is shared and a sibling's commit sweeps whatever you staged (observed twice); (2) never 'git stash' / 'git checkout' / 'git restore' over the working tree — they operate on the WHOLE tree and silently steal every sibling's uncommitted work, then hand it back later (observed once: a migration worker watched its finished file revert to the pre-migration version mid-task). Red-first probes and A/B bisection belong in a temp-dir fixture or a throwaway worktree, never in the shared tree
rationale: two distinct live defects in one parallel wave; both cost attribution or time, neither lost content

decision: PARALLEL GIT SAFETY, amendment: 'git reset' in every form (--soft, --mixed, --hard) joins stash/checkout/restore on the absolute worker prohibition list. Observed live: a worker used reset --soft then reset --hard to undo a polluted commit while five siblings held uncommitted work in the same checkout — the tree survived only because the correction was immediate. A worker that produced a wrong commit reports it and lets MAIN fix history; it never rewrites shared history itself. The four sanctioned worker git verbs are: status, diff, log, and a single path-scoped commit
rationale: third git incident of the wave and the only one with catastrophic potential; content survived, discipline did not

decision: PARALLEL GIT SAFETY, refinement (found by exec-w27): 'git commit -- <paths>' refuses UNTRACKED pathspecs, so a worker creating new files (references, provenance, cell json, report) must first run 'git add -N' — intent-to-add, which registers the path without staging content — on exactly those new paths, then the single atomic path-scoped commit. 'git add -N' is the ONLY add form permitted, scoped to the worker's own new files; plain 'git add' stays forbidden because it stages content a sibling's commit can sweep
rationale: verified live: plain path-scoped commit fails on untracked files even with -o/--only; the -N form kept the commit to exactly 4 files with siblings untouched

decision: PARALLEL GIT SAFETY, canonical technique (found by exec-w25, supersedes the add -N refinement as the preferred form): a worker in a shared checkout commits through its OWN temp index, never the repo's — GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> with read-tree HEAD, update-index --add on exactly its paths, write-tree, commit-tree, update-ref. The shared .git/index is never touched, so no sibling can sweep the worker's paths and the worker can never sweep theirs. 'git add -N' + path-scoped commit remains an acceptable fallback when the temp-index form is unavailable; plain 'git add' and every whole-tree verb (reset/stash/checkout/restore) stay forbidden
rationale: three index-contention incidents in one wave, one with confirmed work loss; the temp-index form removes the shared resource entirely instead of coordinating access to it

decision: A law stated in one place and operationalized in others is audited against its own statement, never against its neighbours: a restatement can carry a precondition the law never had, from birth, and the reader obeys the restatement. Where a tier can be checked, check it - compliance that is the output of a required command survives drift that prose does not.
rationale: bee's concurrency law required a concurrency plan before dispatching anything (R86, and routing-and-contracts.md's MANDATORY CONCURRENCY PLAN). The same law's cell tier never drifted, because there parallelism is the output of a required command (cells schedule) an agent must argue against, not a sentence it must remember. decision: work-language-guard D5+D6: matching is an explicit curated term list plus the identifier shape, applied only to prose outside code blocks, inline code, paths and quoted output; the guard becomes the first code that reads 'quiet', which suppresses the silent-step half only — the internal-term half is never silenced by any setting or bypass level.

decision: Before adopting an existing state field as a new signal, grep every read site of it first; if more than one reader exists, introduce a new inert field instead. A field with N readers grants N behaviours the new signal did not ask for.
rationale: worker-conformance locked reuse of the 'pending' marker as its absence signal; a Gate 2 review wave found that flag short-circuits six refusal sites, so the reuse would have disarmed the red-first tier and the ratio ceiling one slice before the negative controls existed to notice.

decision: Any field written by one cell and read by another owes one test row that crosses the seam with nothing hand-written, plus a mirror where the field is absent. Hand-built fixtures on the reader side stay for breadth but never satisfy this.

decision: A test asserting behaviour under a configuration must read that configuration back through the production accessor and fail if it is not what was seeded, before exercising the behaviour. A conclusion that would also hold without the premise is not evidence for it.
rationale: An advisor consult found every pre-existing bypass row in one suite would pass on a silently-failed config seed, since the door refuses with no setting at all; the 'still opens' mirror proves the row is not welded shut but says nothing about whether the setting was ever read.

decision: Judgment contract adopted: rules split into boundary (hold as written for every role), form (rails for cold workers, recorded-deviation defaults for the orchestrator), and environment-conditioned (check the precondition, take the recorded fallback when absent). Every 'letter = spirit' clause replaced with named-deviation language; AGENTS.md carries the short form, routing-and-contracts the full contract.
rationale: Live evidence 2026-07-30: identical work at equal quality and a fraction of the cost once form rules stopped binding the orchestrator, while every boundary rule that fired (judge, close door, regen ack) earned its keep. Silent deviation stays the defect; judgment widens the path, never the boundary.

decision: proof-economy: (1) verified transcripts are legal proof for tiny/small behavior that is not a public contract and carries no hard-gate flag - the real command plus its decisive output recorded via cells verify; new tests owed only for public contracts, hard-gate flags, and bug repros (repro-first unchanged). (2) Suite rent: a guard suite that has not caught a real defect in 6 months moves out of the local/impacted hot path to the CI/nightly tier by a recorded decision - bee-grooming audits this. (3) Sampled judging: standard-lane semantic judge becomes selective (smell, first slice from a new worker/model, or roughly 1-in-3 sample) with escalation to every-slice after any NEEDS_REVISION; high-risk keeps every-slice; the frozen judge stays universal.
rationale: The test reflex prices every proof as a test and every suite as immortal: ~40 of this repo's 76 suites are harness guards, the slowest four are all meta-tests, and small work pays test-authoring cost that a recorded transcript proves better. Aligned with the Judgment contract: tight on public contracts, hard gates, and bugs; free in between.

decision: Worktree-first routing adopted: code-touching feature work branches at feature start; main checkout is integration/docs/release only; supersedes lane-first deferral
rationale: Owner-approved 2026-07-31 (docs/specs/worktree-first.md): concurrent sessions never share a git index or dirty tree; main stays releasable; landing stays bee worktree merge

decision: Distribution stays source-checkout install: bee is installed per project by running the onboarder (or scripts/install.sh) from a bee source checkout; no public registry shim skill, no network installer flow. Revisit only if bee is ever released publicly.
rationale: Owner decision 2026-07-31: bee serves the owner's own projects where a source checkout is always available; a fluent-style shim entry point solves a distribution problem bee does not have.

decision: Test-simple adopted: one declared test path (commands.test) run by a deterministic bee test runner writing normalized test-results.json; cells finish caps on green, refuses on red with failure_excerpt. The proof-tier matrix, feature-verify-pending deferral, test-cell/feature-verify debt doors, evidence flags, volume brakes, transcript-proof path are deleted. Close doors become tests-green + capture; merge gate keeps commands.verify. Spec: docs/specs/test-simple.md
rationale: Owner 2026-07-31: bee's evidence machinery grew too heavy; fluent's single deterministic path is simpler and sufficient — TDD/red-first/coverage-judgment survive as craft prose, not cap doors.

decision: Capture is deferred like review: close green records capture as pending work (capture queue + uncaptured behavior_change cells are the signal; orient/status keep reminding) and bee-capturing's Compound runs on demand later — never inline as the chain's next step. Same-turn settlement capture (decisions log + capture add stubs) stays immediate. Batching several features into one capture session is sanctioned.
rationale: Owner 2026-07-31: Compound only reads artifacts and rewrites docs, so deferring it speeds delivery; the pending record plus reminders prevent loss.

decision: Prebuilt binaries are published per release and preferred by both installers, superseding 1f4262ca. The release-binaries workflow builds x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc from the tag, publishes them plus SHA256SUMS as release assets, and refuses to publish when .claude-plugin/plugin.json disagrees with the tag. install.sh/install.ps1 download the asset for the host, verify its SHA-256, and pin the cloned source tree to the SAME tag so BEE_VERSION and the vendored instruction layer always come from one commit; any download or checksum failure is non-fatal and falls back to the cargo build, which also remains the path for uncovered platforms and for --build-from-source.
rationale: 1f4262ca kept binaries out of the repo and made every host compile its own, which put a Rust toolchain plus a multi-minute build in front of every install - the largest adoption cost bee had. The original decision's own text scoped it: 'Revisit only if bee is ever released publicly.' Binaries are still absent from the repo; they are built by CI from the tag and attached to the release, so the no-vendored-binary property survives while the install becomes copy-and-wire.

rationale: Three numbering eras coexisted after validation-diet D2: skills said Gates 1-2 + Gate 4, the runtime bypass banners said Gates 1-3 + Gate 4, and the write-guard/claim refusals said Gate 3 (execution). The worst case was a user-facing help string ('Refuses while Gate 3 (execution) is unapproved') that would make an agent surface the wrong gate. decision: The gate-bypass stop net prescribes the MERGED approval —  ee state gate --merge --approved true, not --name execution — and treats Gate 2 as pending unless BOTH shape and xecution are already true.

decision: The Codex Windows hook transport no longer uses Node. commandWindows is now: git -c alias.beehook="!<sh body>" beehook — git runs an exclamation-prefixed alias from the repository TOP LEVEL, so the command string never has to COMPUTE the repo root, which was the sole reason a node -e interpreter survived the R6 Node deletion.
rationale: The old exemption rested on an unexamined premise: the no-dollar/percent/backtick rule (needed so cmd.exe and powershell.exe parse one string identically) bans command substitution, therefore the string cannot ask git for the root, therefore it needs an interpreter. The premise assumed the root must be COMPUTED. It does not — git supplies it. The sh body avoids dollar by unrolling the two candidate binary paths instead of looping over them, and by testing git rev-parse exit status instead of capturing its output; both diagnostics are single-quoted, so the alias value keeps the only pair of double quotes in the string. Measured on Windows 11 / git 2.51.2 across {cmd.exe, powershell.exe} x {repo root, subdirectory, repo with no vendored binary, not a repo}: all 8 either launch the binary or print the correct diagnostic and exit 0. bee now ships one binary and its Windows hook transport needs nothing installed that git did not already require.

decision: Config keys "lanes" and "capabilities" are removed from default_config(), .bee/config.json and both shipped samples. The annotated sample now carries every key bee actually reads: cells_archive_on_close, ship_visibility and worktree_first were added; product_root stays documented-but-unset on purpose.
rationale: Both keys were seeded into every new repo and documented as "reserved - leave {} unless a bee release documents a key", and nothing has ever read either one. A config key with no reader is not a reserved extension point, it is a promise the code does not keep: it invites a host to configure something that cannot take effect, and it makes the sample look complete while four keys that DO have readers were missing from it. Removal is behaviour-neutral for the same reason it is safe - bee ignores unknown top-level keys, so an existing config still carrying them keeps working. The templates test now asserts the exact seeded key set, so a future keyless key cannot slip back in silently.

decision: AskUserQuestion auto-fix emits permissionDecision "ask", never "allow": the question tool's permission prompt IS the question, so an allow verdict pre-approved it away and the tool returned no selection — the asker then fell back to its own default and the human never saw the question. Reverses the emission half of ask-guard-autofix D2; updatedInput rides the ask verdict (documented combination). The write guard's reservation-warning branch drops its permissionDecision entirely for the same reason: an advisory notice must not double as a pre-approval — the warning now rides additionalContext + systemMessage and the write takes the ordinary permission flow.
rationale: Observed live: a 13-char header ("Product field") tripped the auto-fix, the guard emitted allow+updatedInput, and the question was skipped with no answer. Verified after the fix by rebuilding .bee/bin/bee.exe and asking a real 16-char-header question in-session: the header truncated to "Reservation…", the prompt rendered, and the user answered.

decision: model-guard derives and repairs instead of refusing: (1) subagent_type bee-gather/bee-extract/bee-review IS a tier declaration — the agent file is rendered from that tier's configured model, so a dispatch naming one needs no marker and no model param (additive: fires only where the guard previously had nothing to go on); (2) a declared tier riding subagent_type "general-purpose" is rewritten to the tier's pinned type via updatedInput instead of denied; (3) a declared tier disagreeing with an explicit model param is rewritten to the tier's configured model — AO5 already named config the winner, so there was nothing left to ask. Still refused: bare dispatch, unconfigured model, model param on a nameless tier, cli-resolved tier. Repairs carry no permissionDecision (hook-runtime R23) and are announced via additionalContext + systemMessage; transports generic-type-repaired / param-tier-repaired / pinned-type keep the audit honest.
rationale: Measured on this repo: 126 of 399 dispatches refused (32%), 104 of them the marker + general-purpose pairing, 98 in a single day. Every one of those was the guard demanding a value it could derive, handed back to the actor that had just guessed wrong — the bare-deny FIX even routed callers into the next refusal by naming the marker without naming the agent type. Reversal of the AO5/AO10 deny arm, not of its authority order.

decision: Hook wiring resolves the bee binary at HOOK time with a MAIN-CHECKOUT fallback, and the vendored-binary fast path is retired. Every projection (claude repo settings.json, claude plugin manifest, codex repo POSIX) now runs: direct candidates under $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR / $r, then — only if those miss — g=$(git -C <dir> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) and $g/../.bee/bin/bee[.exe]. repo_hook_command no longer renders the short "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.bee/bin/bee.exe form when a binary is present at onboard time: that form is not a candidate a runner can fall past, it is a nonexistent command, so no fallback could sit behind it. rationale: A linked git worktree materialises tracked files only and the binary is untracked by decision 1f4262ca, so every worktree had all 11 hooks wired to a path that does not exist; each took its fail-open arm and exited 0 — no gate enforcement, no reservations, no tier guard, no session preamble — and nothing could report it because the reporter is the missing binary. Measured on git 2.51.2 from a linked worktree: --show-toplevel returns the worktree, --git-common-dir returns the main .git. Verified end-to-end by running the rendered write-guard command inside a binary-less worktree: it reached the main checkout and returned a real verdict. Codex WINDOWS leg is a named gap — its git-alias transport bans $, so it cannot capture command output.

decision: bee onboard --repo-root . --apply is UNSAFE to run from inside a feature worktree: it silently overwrites the worktree's AGENTS.md with the MAIN checkout's AGENTS.block.md, destroying uncommitted edits, and reports neither changes_needed nor blocked_*. Until onboard's source resolution is fixed, a cell that edits AGENTS.block.md inside a worktree must verify the spliced result after --apply and restore its edit if the block was reverted.
rationale: Found while executing cell dvl-2 on 2026-08-05. Engine::locate() in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/onboard/source.rs resolves its source root exe-dir-first, walking from current_exe() AFTER symlink resolution. A worktree's .bee/bin/bee is a symlink into the main checkout, so locate() always resolves the MAIN checkout as the template source, no matter which root --repo-root names. The worker's edited AGENTS.block.md was in the worktree; the block spliced into AGENTS.md came from main; the edit vanished with no signal. The worker recovered by forcing BEE_JS_ENTRY at a synthetic worktree path, which is a workaround, not a fix.
alternatives: Blocking the command inside a worktree outright was considered, but onboard --apply is exactly what a worktree cell owes when it touches a manifest-hashed root, so a hard refusal would deadlock that cell. The real fix is for locate() to prefer --repo-root over the exe directory.

decision: knowledge-loop D1: bee knowledge context --work <id> and bee knowledge promote --work <id> accept a feature slug that has NO bee.work-item concept. No work-item file is ever auto-created. unknown_work stays the typed error only when neither a work-item concept nor any history anchor exists.
rationale: Only 2 bee.work-item concepts exist across ~41 features, and --work is the mandatory join key for both the retrieval ranker and promote, so the whole knowledge read path is unreachable for 39 features. Auto-authoring a work-item stub would either fabricate title/description prose (forbidden by D10 -- a fabricated summary reads as curated and gets trusted) or leave a per-feature file to tend. CONTEXT.md already carries the feature's locked decisions in the feature's own words, so it is the honest anchor that already exists everywhere.

decision: knowledge-loop D2: bee close runs bee knowledge promote for the closing feature after the tests door reports green and after the scribing-debt door passes. It prints the proposal headline into close output and writes the full proposals to docs/history/<slug>/promote-proposals.md. This is a SOFT door: it never refuses close, and a promote failure degrades to a named warning line. Rather than re-grade 87 concepts by hand, make the flag harmless by ranking within it: the digest is the only knowledge surface every session actually reads, and the ranker it needs already exists and measures well (AUC 0.805, zero_signal 0 on the live bundle). decision: worktree-reclaim D1: bee worktree merge runs its cleanup path BY DEFAULT on a green (or verify-skipped) merge — worktree directory, branch, grant and workspace record all go. A no-cleanup flag opts one merge out; the .bee/config.json key worktree_cleanup_on_merge (default true) opts a repo out. The old cleanup flag stays accepted as a no-op for compatibility. Cleanup still refuses on a dirty worktree, a textual conflict, or a red verify — unchanged.
rationale: Cleanup was opt-in, so nobody passed it: 13 dead worktrees held 4.5GB on this machine with every branch already ahead=0 against main. Opt-in cleanup makes leaking the default outcome.
alternatives: Leave the default and only add a prune command — rejected: it cleans the old leak but not the new one.

decision: worktree-reclaim D2: a new subcommand bee worktree prune sweeps DEAD worktrees the merge path never reclaimed. Dead means all of: the branch is fully merged into the base ref (rev-list --count base..branch is 0), the tree holds no tracked-modified and no untracked files, no live session is bound to it, and its last commit is older than an age threshold. It drops all four artifacts per worktree: directory, branch (branch -d, never -D), grant, workspace record. It carries a dry-run flag and an age-threshold flag, and reports one line per worktree with the reason it was kept or removed.
rationale: A worktree abandoned without going through bee worktree merge is never reclaimed by D1's default. Prune is the sweep that catches what the merge door misses, and it must be safe enough to run unattended.

decision: worktree-reclaim D3: bee worktree unregister drops the workspace record (.bee/runtime/workspaces/<id>.json) in the same call it drops the grant. Today only merge cleanup calls ws::unregister_workspace, so unregister leaves an orphan record behind.
rationale: Observed live on 2026-08-05: unregistering all 13 worktrees emptied worktree-grants.json to {} and left 13 orphan workspace records. A partial teardown leaves the registry lying about what exists.

decision: worktree-reclaim D4: bee orient and the session preamble surface reclaimable worktrees as named open work once the count crosses a threshold, the same way orphaned scribing debt and unapplied promote proposals are surfaced today. The line names the count and the reclaimable size, and the command that reclaims it.
rationale: The leak was invisible until the user measured the disk by hand. State that costs 4.5GB must announce itself at session start, not wait to be discovered.

decision: worktree-reclaim D2a: every probe the prune classifier makes FAILS CLOSED — a missing, unreadable, or non-zero-exit answer keeps the worktree, never removes it. Mergedness is tested with git merge-base --is-ancestor (exit-code only), never a parsed rev-list count. The base ref must resolve or the whole run refuses. D2 gains three more keep-conditions: HEAD must be attached and equal to the recorded branch (detached-HEAD commits have no ref and their only reflog dies with the directory); the worktree must hold no in-progress rebase, cherry-pick, merge, or bisect state; and it must hold neither .bee/HANDOFF.json nor a non-empty .bee/capture-queue.jsonl. Prune uses its own liveness window measured in hours, not the 15-minute claim-stealing constant, and treats an unreadable session record as LIVE.
rationale: An adversarial pass proved the plan safety argument false. branch -d protects commits on the branch and nothing else: git worktree remove runs FIRST (merge.rs:307 before :318) and deletes ignored files, detached-HEAD commits, and the per-worktree reflog that was their last reference. The codebase existing fail-open convention (git.rs:113) was written for guards whose failure mode is a retry; deletion has no retry.
alternatives: Reuse branch_exists status-only read for a count that lives in stdout — rejected: one unwrap_or(0) turns any git failure into merged for every worktree at once.

decision: worktree-reclaim D2b: liveness is read from the session records under the main checkout, never from the workspace record. A worktree is held when any session record names it with a fresh heartbeat, OR when a live session resolved root sits under the worktree root. Ownership fields in .bee/runtime/workspaces/*.json are not a liveness signal.
rationale: Verified on disk: all 14 worktree records carry write_owner_session null and attached_sessions empty, including the worktree this session was running inside. The only production caller of claim_write_ownership hardcodes workspace_id = main (state_group/policy.rs:128), so nothing ever writes ownership into a worktree record. Reading it would have degraded D2 to a three-condition test silently, and dry-run would have printed the same wrong reason.

decision: worktree-reclaim D1a: cleanup-by-default fires ONLY on a merge that actually merged something. The ALREADY_UP_TO_DATE arm keeps today behavior and removes nothing. A non-boolean value on the no-cleanup flag is refused outright, never ignored and never delegated.
rationale: phases.rs:240 routes the zero-work merge through the same attach_cleanup_outcome call as the green merge. Under a default-on flip, re-running merge to check status would delete the worktree, and a worktree with an hour of uncommitted gitignored work reads as clean plus trivially merged. Today a mis-parsed cleanup flag means the favour was not done; after the flip a mis-parsed no-cleanup flag means deleted anyway.

decision: worktree-reclaim D3a: the shared teardown helper takes directory removal as an explicit non-default parameter and asserts the current directory is not inside the tree it is about to remove. bee worktree unregister reaches only the registry half — grant, workspace record, holds release — never the directory.
rationale: run_unregister defaults its id to the CURRENT worktree when run from inside one (registry.rs:238) and, unlike run_merge, carries no ordinary-checkout refusal. Wiring it to a teardown helper that can remove directories would recreate the self-delete that run_merge kind check exists to prevent (handlers.rs:427).

decision: worktree-reclaim D4a (AMENDS D4): the session-preamble line names the count of reclaimable worktrees and the command, but NOT the reclaimable size, and it runs no git subprocess at session start. Size is computed inside bee worktree prune, where the user asked for it and already pays for a scan. The preamble line is derived from filesystem facts alone.
rationale: D4 as locked would put N git rev-list plus N status --porcelain spawns and a walk of 4.5GB of target/ on the session-start critical path. This repo already measured and fixed that exact regression: bee orient 850ms with the git-candidate file, 280ms with it emptied (status_full/records.rs:477). The preamble also holds about 279 bytes of headroom against its 5120-byte budget (session_preamble/budget.rs:61), pinned by a test. The count and the command carry the whole message; the size does not survive its cost.
alternatives: Cache the size on disk and refresh it in prune — rejected for now as a second store to keep honest for one number the prune output already prints.

decision: worktree-reclaim D5: packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/generated/registry_payload.json is hand-edited in this repo, with the reason recorded, because its declared regen chain does not exist here. Every cell that adds or changes a CLI command edits the payload directly and re-runs tests/registry_contracts.rs plus tests/registry_dispatch.rs as the proof.
rationale: tests/registry_contracts.rs:157 names the chain as node scripts/export_registry_payload.mjs, but scripts/ holds only install.sh and install.ps1, and the repo contains zero .mjs/.js/.ts files outside target and node_modules. The rule presupposes an environment fact that is absent, so it takes its recorded fallback instead of demanding the ritual. Two mechanics ride along: the payload is a single 168KB line, so any edit diffs as one changed line; and registry examples are EXECUTED by tests/registry_dispatch.rs:131 in a scratch dir that is not a git repo, so a new command example must be inert and must not print a refusal marker.

decision: Orchestrating a worktree feature from one session requires alternating checkouts: bee dispatch prepare, decisions log and state set all refuse inside a granted worktree, while a dispatched subagent inherits the session cwd and the write guard refuses cross-worktree writes. A granted worktree also has no .bee/bin/bee, so workers must call the main checkout's binary by absolute path.

Separately, state set --feature on the default record delegates to a Node runtime this repo no longer ships, so switching the default record's feature is impossible — the working path is state start-feature --as-lane followed by state session bind --session-id.

decision: CONTEXT.md's claim that one prune run clears the 13 orphan workspace records is WRONG, verified against the shipped code. Their directories and branches were both removed by hand earlier in the session, so merge-base --is-ancestor cannot exit 0 for a branch that does not exist, and D2a's fail-closed rule correctly reads that as not-provably-merged and keeps them. Every one of the 13 is kept forever. The follow-up is a distinct verdict: when a record's worktree directory is absent AND its branch is absent, the record is the only artifact left, so dropping it loses nothing and is safe without any merge test.
rationale: Ran bee worktree prune --dry-run against the freshly built binary: all 13 report kept with the same not-provably-merged reason. The fail-closed rule is behaving as designed; the defect is that the orphan-record case was never given a verdict of its own. Naming it beats quietly widening the merge test, which would reopen the deletion risk D2a exists to close.

decision: Gate 2 (merged) for windows-shell-doctrine is recorded APPROVED under gate_bypass=total, not by the user. Approved shape: onboarding appends a Windows Environment section to the managed AGENTS.md block when the resolved host shell is powershell — .bee/config.json host_shell wins, else cfg!(windows). The section states the two-shell split (user terminal = PowerShell, agent Bash tool and the ! prefix = Git Bash), the PowerShell default for anything handed to the user, and the three Windows facts that break silently: forward-slash paths in Bash-tool commands, CRLF, and NTFS exec-bit/symlink semantics.

The config key makes the shell a property of the REPO, recorded once, with host detection as the default so no project has to set anything. Shipping it unconditionally was rejected — every Linux project would carry a section claiming it runs on Windows.

decision: A host-dependent doctrine section is decided by the REPOSITORY first and the machine second: onboarding reads .bee/config.json host_shell (powershell|posix) and only falls back to the running host when the key is absent or unrecognised. The Windows Environment section ships this way, rendered inside the managed AGENTS.md block.
rationale: Pure host detection churns a shared repo — a Linux teammate's onboard --apply strips the section and the next Windows run restores it, so the file oscillates in git. Making the shell a recorded property of the project ends that, while host fallback keeps the key optional. An unrecognised value falls back rather than refusing, so a typo never blocks onboarding. Proven live: a fixture repo with host_shell=powershell rendered '## Environment — Windows' inside the markers, flipping it to posix removed it, and a second run reported up_to_date.
